thread.title: Costco Crumbles, Tesla Slides as Dow Dips on Jobs Disappointment

title: Costco Crumbles, Tesla Slides as Dow Dips on Jobs Disappointment
text:
Costco Crumbles, Tesla Slides as Dow Dips on Jobs Disappointment By Oct. 5, 2018 8:55 a.m. ET Order Reprints Michael Haddad Text size
Disappointing . The Dow Jones Industrial Average, which ended decidedly in the red on Thursday as the 10-year Treasury yield rose to multiyear highs , was slipping after the U.S. added just 134,000 jobs in September. Costco was slumping after warning about its financial reporting, while Tesla was lower after a judge asked CEO Elon Musk and SEC to explain their settlement . In today’s morning movers, we… …look ahead to earnings season; …explain why Snap is gaining; …and highlight a downgrade to HP Inc. Barron’s Briefs Talk about disappointing . The U.S. added just 134,000 jobs in September , well below forecasts for 185,000. The unemployment rate, however, fell to 3.7%, a 49-year low, while average hourly earnings rose 2.8% from a year ago, in line with expectations. The report isn’t helping the market any. S&P 500 futures have declined 0.1%, while Dow Jones Industrial futures have dipped 25 points, or 0.1%, and Nasdaq Composite futures have fallen 0.3%. Overnight, Southeast Asian markets (I.e. the Nikkei, Hang Seng and KOSPI) c losed lower for the either the third or fourth straight day. The Bloomberg hack story continues to ripple through the tech economy. For example, Japanese electronic test supplier Advantest was down 4% and Chinese based Lenovo dropped 15%. The market appears to be in the ‘shoot first and ask questions later’ mode of operations—denials by Super Micro (SMCI), Apple (AAPL) and Amazon.com (AMZN) haven’t been enough to stem the tide of negative tech sentiment . It’s just about time to start thinking about earnings . Next week the banks report numbers and can opine on the direction of rates and how that will impact loan growth and housing markets. Don’t forget that banks have lagged behind the broader market on a 1-year and YTD basis—apparently a flattening yield curve has weighed on sentiment. Next Friday is also another chance for Wells Fargo (WFC) to address its reputational issues . Regarding Industrials, Fastenal (FAST) has been the poster child for the theme of US-centric manufacturing and tax reform; it’s up 27% year over year. FAST reports numbers Wednesday and the direction of margins will be a focus for investors. The Yankees and Red Sox start their ALDS Series in Boston today . Remember, “Manny being Manny” in reference to the antics of Manny Ramirez who was an odd-duck, but a transcendent right-handed hitter? Now we have “Elon being Elon.” The transcendently talented engineer tweeted at the SEC last night implying the regulator works at the behest of short sellers. Tesla’s (TSLA) shares are off 2.8% at $273.89 in pre-open trading. Analyst upgrades and downgrades look themeless . A little of this and little of that. CIBC launched on several Canadian energy stocks. Cenovus Energy (CVE), Suncor Energy (SU) and Canadian Natural Resources (CNQ) are the buys and Imperial Oil (IMO) is rated underperform (I.e. it’s the sell). Morning Movers
Costco Wholesale (COST) is down 2.7% to $225.33 after reporting fourth-quarter earnings . The discounter earned $2.36 a share on revenue of $44.41 billion. Analysts were expecting earnings of $2.34 a share on revenue of $44.17 billion. However, it warned it will report material weakness in internal financial control in its coming 10K. That said, Moody’s also upgraded Costco’s debt, to Aa3.
HP Inc . (HPQ) is down 1.7% to $25.96 after JPMorgan downgraded it to Neutral.
Lowe’s (LOW) is down 0.7% to $110 after naming a new interim chief financial officer .
Snap (SNAP) is up 3.3% to $8.06 after its CEO set a goal of profitability in 2019 in a memo to employees .
Tesla (TSLA) is down 2.9% to $273.61 after CEO Elon Musk couldn’t help himself, and tweeted about the Securities and Exchange Commission , just days after reaching a settlement with the agency. —Teresa Rivas Costco Crumbles, Tesla Slides as Dow Dips on Jobs Disappointment Disappointing.
